videos.titulo: What it is and how to read it

cenas.sub: What it is and how to read every element

cenas.texto: The cross gives the direction. The star gives the launch pad.
cenas.fala: Hi, I'm Ricardo Garcia, and this is the RocketNova Bootcamp. RocketNova is the trend scanner from MoreThanMoney, written from scratch with our own code. Before we start, one idea that will run through both videos: the moving average cross gives the direction, but on its own it is not enough. The signal is only born when there is a recent star on the right side, the launch pad. And when it is born, it brings the full plan drawn on the candle: entry, stop and four targets. This bootcamp is short and practical. In the first video we look at what RocketNova is and how to read every element on the chart. In the second we cover the signal, the plan, the management the indicator does by itself, the cases where you do not enter, and a routine to practise on a demo account. The goal is that you can read the indicator before you risk a single cent. Let's go.

itens: Video 1 · What RocketNova is and how to read it
Video 2 · Signal, plan, management and routine
cenas.fala: The bootcamp has two videos. This first one is the map: what RocketNova is, what the three moving averages mean, the stars, the Rocket Candle, and the two panels that sit in the corner of the chart. The second is the practice: how a full signal is born, how the plan is drawn, what the indicator does by itself after the entry, when not to enter, and a simple routine to practise on demo. Watch the videos in order. The second one assumes you already recognise everything that appears in this first one. Do not worry about memorising numbers. Worry about recognising each piece of the chart, and about separating clearly what is context from what is a signal. That is the work of this video.

cenas.sub: Trend with structure and a fixed plan
cenas.fala: Chapter one. What is RocketNova, after all?

cenas.titulo: With the trend, from a launch pad
itens: Trend following with three exponential moving averages: 20, 50 and 238
The signal is born on the confirmed cross of the 20 over the 50
By default it requires a recent star on the right side
The Rocket Candle shows impulse; the pulse and the clock show context
Entry, stop and four targets are fixed on the signal candle
cenas.fala: RocketNova is the MoreThanMoney indicator for TradingView that follows the trend. It reads the market with three exponential moving averages: the twenty, the fifty and the two hundred and thirty-eight. The signal is born when the fast one crosses the slow one and the candle closes. But the cross alone is not enough. By default, a buy requires a recent swing low star, and a sell requires a swing high star. That is what we call the launch pad: the market made an extreme, took a breath, and now the averages turn in the same direction. Around this there are three context readings: the Rocket Candle, which is the impulse candle, the Volatility Pulse, which tells you whether the market is alive or flat, and the Trade Clock, which tells you whether you are in session and with volume. And when the signal appears, the plan is fixed on the candle right away: entry, stop and four targets. None of this is prediction. It is reading structure, with a plan decided before you enter.

cenas.sub: Averages, colours, stars, Rocket Candle, labels and panels
cenas.fala: Chapter two. Let's read every element on the chart, one at a time.

cenas.titulo: Three averages and the candle colours
cenas.fala: This chart is illustrative. It is here to explain how the indicator is read; it is not a real result or market history. I say this once in this bootcamp and it applies to every chart. First, the three averages. The red one is the twenty period exponential moving average, the fastest. The blue one is the fifty. The orange one, thicker, is the two hundred and thirty-eight, the long average, which tells you the side of the bigger market. Now look at the candle colours. When the twenty is above the fifty, the candles turn green: uptrend. When it is below, they turn orange: downtrend. You do not need to measure anything. The candle colour is the fastest reading of direction, and the order of the averages confirms it.

The stars are the swing highs and lows that the indicator confirms. A green star below a candle marks a low. A red star above marks a high. For a low to be a star it has to dominate thirty-four candles to the left, the Depth setting, and be confirmed by eight candles to the right, the Backstep. That is why the star always appears with a delay: you only see it eight candles after the extreme. And there is also the Deviation: the star has to be at least one point three ATR away from the previous opposite star, so it does not mark noise. Fix this idea: the green star is the floor the rocket can lift off from. For a buy, the signal will require a green star within the last forty candles. For a sell, a red star.

itens: A candle with a body of at least one point two ATR
Closes at the extreme: the wick on the closing side is small
Painted yellow on the chart
By default it is information, not a requirement
With the filter on, it must appear in the five candles before the signal
cenas.fala: The Rocket Candle is the impulse candle. For a candle to be a Rocket Candle, the body has to measure at least one point two times the fourteen period ATR, and it has to close near the extreme: on a bullish candle, the upper wick is small; on a bearish candle, the lower wick is small. When it happens, the candle turns yellow, and it stands out among the green and orange ones. By default, the Rocket Candle is information. It tells you there is strength in the move, but it is not required for the signal. If you turn the filter on in the settings, it becomes required: the indicator only signals if there is a Rocket Candle in the same direction within the five candles before the cross. It is a way of asking the market for more conviction, at the cost of fewer signals.

Now let's look at a sell. At the top, a red star appears: the market made a high and confirmed it. A few candles later, the twenty average crosses below the fifty, the candle closes, and the indicator draws the Sell label above the candle. That label is the full signal. It only appears when the cross has closed, when the right star is within the last forty candles, and when the Trade Clock is inside the session. Notice that the star and the label are different things. The star is the launch pad. The label is the launch. A buy is the mirror image: green star below, cross upwards, Buy label below the candle. And it is on the label candle that the indicator fixes the plan, which we will see in the second video.

In the right corner of the chart there are two panels. The first is the Volatility Pulse. It compares the fourteen period ATR with its hundred candle average. If the ATR is at one point three times the average or more, it reads HIGH, the market is agitated. If it is at zero point seven or less, it reads LOW, the market is flat, and targets take long to arrive. In between, it reads NORMAL. The second panel is the Trade Clock. It shows whether you are inside the trading session, which by default runs from eight in the morning to nine at night, and whether volume is healthy. Good Volume is what you want to see. Low Volume means the candle's volume is below half the average. Market Closed means you are outside the session, and there the indicator does not even give signals, unless you allow it in the settings.

cenas.sub: Trend, star, impulse, pulse and clock
cenas.fala: Chapter three. The five confirmations you read before thinking about entering.

itens: Trend: the EMA 20 crossed the 50 and the candle closed
Launch star on the right side within the last 40 candles
Rocket Candle in the same direction, if the filter is on
Volatility Pulse at NORMAL or HIGH
Trade Clock inside the session and at Good Volume
cenas.fala: Let's put it all in one list. One, the trend: the twenty average crossed the fifty and the candle closed. If you turn on the long average filter, buys only count above the two hundred and thirty-eight and sells only below. Two, the launch star: a recent low for a buy, or a recent high for a sell, within the last forty candles. Three, the Rocket Candle: an impulse candle in the same direction in the last few candles, required only if you have the filter on. Four, the Volatility Pulse at NORMAL or HIGH. At LOW, the market is flat. Five, the Trade Clock inside the session and at Good Volume. The first two are the ones the indicator requires to draw the label. The other three are context you read yourself. The indicator does the mechanical part. The decision is still yours.

cartoes.d: Direction. Green with the 20 above the 50, orange with the 20 below.
The launch pad. Green at a low, red at a high, confirmed eight candles later.
The impulse. Yellow candle with a 1.2 ATR body closing at the extreme.
The context. Volatility Pulse and Trade Clock, in the right corner.

cenas.fala: Four pieces, four roles. The averages and the candle colour give you direction. The star gives you the launch pad, the extreme the move can lift off from. The Rocket Candle gives you the impulse, the proof that there is strength in the move. And the panels give you context: whether the market is alive and whether you are at the right time. When you look at a chart with RocketNova, always do this reading in the same order. Direction, launch pad, impulse, context. After a few days, you do it in seconds. And it is that quick reading that lets you recognise a good signal and let a weak one pass, without hesitation.

cenas.cap: 04 · What the chart does not tell you
cenas.titulo: What the chart does not tell you
cenas.fala: Chapter four. What the chart does not tell you, and the mistakes to avoid from the start.

cenas.cap: 04 · What the chart does not tell you
itens: Entering on the cross before the candle closes
Treating the star as if it were the signal
Ignoring the Trade Clock and trading at Market Closed
Forgetting the Volatility Pulse at LOW
Moving the stop after the plan is drawn
cenas.fala: Five common mistakes. First, entering on the cross before the candle closes. The averages can cross and uncross inside the same candle; the indicator only confirms on the close, and so do you. Second, treating the star as if it were the signal. The star is the launch pad, not the launch. Third, ignoring the Trade Clock. Outside the session, volume is weak and false moves are more frequent. Fourth, forgetting the Volatility Pulse at LOW: a flat market gives repeated crosses with no follow-through. Fifth, and the most expensive: moving the stop after the plan is drawn. The plan is fixed on the signal candle for a reason. If the market did not want it, accept the stop and wait for the next launch.

cenas.cap: 04 · What the chart does not tell you
itens: Open RocketNova on US30 or gold, on five or fifteen minutes
Find ten Buy or Sell labels and the star that preceded each one
Note the Volatility Pulse and Trade Clock colour on each
Do not trade yet. Just read.
cenas.fala: Before the second video, do this. Open RocketNova on a five or fifteen minute chart, on US30 or gold. Scroll back through the history and find ten Buy or Sell labels. For each one, find the star that preceded it and count how many candles passed between the star and the label. Note how the Volatility Pulse and the Trade Clock looked on that candle. And note whether there was a Rocket Candle in the candles before. Do not trade yet, not even on demo. This exercise has one goal only: after ten labels, you look at the chart and see the full sequence before it happens. Direction, launch pad, impulse, context. In the second video we move on to the plan and the management.

cenas.titulo: From the cross to the decision
itens: The full sequence of a signal
The plan: entry, stop and four targets
The management the indicator does by itself
When not to enter
A routine to practise on demo
cenas.fala: Welcome to the second video of the RocketNova Bootcamp. In the first one you learned to read every piece of the chart. Now we move to the decision. We will see the full sequence of a signal, from the cross to the label. Then, the plan that is drawn on the candle: entry, stop and four targets. Next, the management the indicator does by itself: the stop that moves to entry after the first target, and the opposite signal that closes the trade. We will also see the cases where you do not enter, and a simple routine for your session on a demo account. The indicator is mechanical. Your preparation has to be even calmer than it is.

cenas.titulo: From the cross to the signal
cenas.fala: Chapter one. How a signal is born, from start to finish.

cenas.rotulo: Buy · plan fixed on the candle
cenas.fala: Let's look at a buy, step by step. The market was falling, made a low, and eight candles later the indicator confirms that low with a green star. That is the launch pad. Meanwhile a yellow candle appears, a Rocket Candle: the impulse is in our favour. The candles go from orange to green, because the twenty average crossed above the fifty. The candle closes inside the session, there is a green star within the last forty candles, and the indicator draws the Buy label below the candle. At the same instant, it draws the plan: the golden entry line, the red zone down to the stop, and the green zone with the four targets. All fixed on the signal candle. From here on there is nothing left to decide on the chart. There is only the plan to follow.

itens: Read the direction from the candle colour and the order of the averages
Confirm the star on the right side within the last 40 candles
Wait for the closed cross inside the Trade Clock
Read the Volatility Pulse, the volume and the Rocket Candle
Size the position by the risk to the stop, and only then enter
cenas.fala: The sequence, in order. One: you read the direction, from the candle colour and the order of the averages. Two: you confirm there is a star on the right side within the last forty candles. Three: you wait for the closed cross, inside the Trade Clock. Four: you read the context, the Volatility Pulse, the volume state, and whether there is a Rocket Candle in your favour. Five: you size the position by the risk to the stop the indicator drew. Only after this does the order go to the broker, at the Entry label price. If any step fails, the trade does not exist, however good the chart looks. This discipline is what separates following an indicator from gambling with it.
Chapter two. The plan that is fixed on the signal candle.

cenas.titulo: A hundred pip stop, four targets
linhas: A hundred pips (two hundred on gold), or the last opposite star
One hundred percent of the stop
One hundred and fifty percent of the stop
cenas.fala: The plan has six lines. The entry is the close of the signal candle, the price on the Entry label. The stop, by default, is fixed: a hundred pips on most pairs and indices, two hundred on gold. On US30, a hundred pips is a hundred index points. The four targets are measured from the stop distance. TP1 sits at thirty percent of that distance, TP2 at fifty, or sixty on gold, TP3 at one hundred percent, and TP4 at one hundred and fifty. The green zone runs from the entry to the last target, the red zone from the entry to the stop. The box stays drawn for twenty candles. Before you send the order, size the position with the risk you decided for the account. The indicator draws the plan, but the lot size is always yours to set.

itens: Fixed Points: a hundred pips, two hundred on gold, or the value you set
Structure: at the last opposite star, with a 0.2 ATR buffer
With a structure stop, the targets scale in the same proportion
Without an available star, the indicator falls back to the fixed stop
cenas.fala: The stop has two modes in the settings. The first is Fixed Points: a fixed distance, a hundred pips by default, two hundred on gold, or a value you set yourself. The second is Structure. Here the stop sits at the last star on the opposite side: on a buy, at the green star of the low; on a sell, at the red star of the high. The indicator adds a buffer of zero point two ATR beyond the star, so a wick does not catch it. With a structure stop, the targets scale in the same proportion: if the stop is shorter, the targets come closer; if it is wider, the targets move further away. And if there is no star available, the indicator falls back to the fixed stop. Pick one mode and keep it. Changing the rule halfway through a week is the fastest way to learn nothing from your journal.

cenas.sub: Targets, stop at entry and opposite signal
cenas.fala: Chapter three. What happens after the entry, and what the indicator does by itself.

cenas.rotulo: Management · TP1 and stop at entry
cenas.fala: Watch the management on the chart. The buy entered at the Buy label, with the stop down below, in red. Price rises and touches TP1. Two things happen here: you close part of the position, and the indicator moves the stop to the entry, the golden line. From this candle on, the trade no longer loses. If price comes back to the entry, it exits with a BE, break-even. Then price touches TP2, TP3 and TP4, and at each one you close another part. When the last target is touched, the trade is over. Notice there are no decisions in the middle. The plan was drawn before, and the management follows fixed rules. All you have to do is execute the partials when price touches each line.

itens: After TP1 the stop moves to the entry
Each target touched marks an event: TP1, TP2, TP3, TP4
Stop touched before TP1 is SL; after TP1 it is BE
An opposite signal closes whatever is left of the trade
Everything goes out as an alert with the same id, ready for a webhook
cenas.fala: The indicator manages the trade with four rules. First: after TP1 the stop moves to the entry. Second: each target touched marks an event, TP1, TP2, TP3, TP4, in order. Third: if the stop is touched before TP1 it is an SL; if it is touched after TP1, with the stop already at entry, it is a BE. Fourth: an opposite signal closes whatever is left of the trade and opens the new one. All of this goes out as an alert, with the same identifier as the entry. That is what feeds the RocketNova signals chat and Tap to Trade in the MoreThanMoney app: the entry arrives with direction, entry, stop and the four targets, and the follow-ups arrive after it. The management is mechanical on purpose. Your job is not to spoil it.

cartoes.d: US30 and NAS100 on five or fifteen minutes. A hundred pip stop by default.
XAUUSD. Two hundred pip stop and TP2 at sixty percent.
Major pairs. A hundred pip stop by default.
Bitcoin and high volume pairs. Check the Volatility Pulse.

cenas.fala: Where it is used. On indices, US30 and NAS100 on five or fifteen minutes are the main example, with the hundred pip stop by default. On gold, the indicator adjusts by itself: the stop becomes two hundred pips and TP2 moves to sixty percent. On the major forex pairs, the hundred pip stop applies the same way. On crypto, Bitcoin and the high volume pairs work, but always check the Volatility Pulse, because volatility changes a lot from one day to the next. For swing, you can use one hour or four hours, with the same rules. Whatever the asset, start with just one. Learn its rhythm before you open more charts.

cenas.sub: Sideways, no star, out of hours
cenas.fala: Chapter four. The cases where the best trade is not to enter.

This is the example that costs you. The market is sideways: the twenty and fifty averages are glued together and cross every few candles. Every cross with a recent star gives a label. The sells reach the first targets, the stop moves to entry, and price turns back: they end at BE, with no real distance travelled. If they were still open, the opposite signal would close them with an exit. And notice the cross in the middle, with no recent star on the right side: there the indicator does not even draw a label. Look at the panel: the Volatility Pulse is at LOW. That is the indicator telling you the market is flat. When you see back-to-back crosses, small candles, and the pulse at LOW, the answer is not to enter. Wait for the market to make a clear extreme, for a star to appear, a Rocket Candle, and for the averages to separate. The indicator will give labels in a sideways market, because the mechanical rules are met. Letting them pass is your part of the job.

itens: A cross with no recent star, or with the star on the wrong side
Trade Clock at Market Closed or Low Volume
Volatility Pulse at LOW with price glued to the averages
Against the EMA 238 without a clear reason
High impact news in the next few minutes
You already have a trade open on the same asset
cenas.fala: The no-entry cases. A cross with no recent star, or with the star on the wrong side: the indicator does not even give a label, and you do not enter either. Trade Clock at Market Closed or at Low Volume. Volatility Pulse at LOW with price glued to the averages. An entry against the two hundred and thirty-eight average without a clear reason, because you are fighting the bigger market. High impact news in the next few minutes, because the hundred pip stop can be hit in a single candle. And when you already have a trade open on the same asset: the indicator closes it on the opposite signal, but two positions at the same time on the same chart is double the risk. Letting a trade pass is not losing a trade. It is protecting the capital for the next launch.
Chapter five. A simple routine to practise on a demo account.

itens: Before the session: one asset, the side of the EMA 238, the recent stars
During: wait for the label and read the panels before entering
Size by the risk to the stop, always the same per trade
Partials at each target, stop at entry after TP1
At the end: record every trade in the journal, taken or not
cenas.fala: The routine. Before the session, open a single asset. Read the side of the long average, the two hundred and thirty-eight, and mark the recent stars. During the session, do not go looking for anything: wait for the label to appear, and when it does, read the panels and the Rocket Candle before deciding. Size by the risk to the stop, and always use the same risk per trade, half a percent or one percent of the account. After entering, execute the partials at each target and let the indicator move the stop to entry at TP1. At the end of the session, record every trade in the journal: the time, the asset, the state of the panels, the result in R. And record the signals you did not take, and why. After four weeks on demo, the journal tells you whether you are ready for a live account. It is not the indicator that decides that. It is your record.

cenas.texto: The cross gives the direction. Discipline gives the result.
cenas.fala: We have reached the end of the RocketNova Bootcamp. To recap: three averages give the direction, the star gives the launch pad, the Rocket Candle shows the impulse, and the panels tell you whether the market is alive and whether you are at the right time. The signal is born on the closed cross next to a star, and the plan is fixed on the candle: entry, stop and four targets. After TP1 the stop moves to entry, and an opposite signal closes the trade. The indicator does the mechanical part. Discipline, position size and the journal are your part. Practise on demo, follow the process, and see you in the MoreThanMoney community chat.
